content.value_statement: Broken JSON blocks API testing and configuration work. This skill validates, formats, fixes, converts, and explains JSON issues with clear guidance.
actual_capabilities: Validates JSON syntax and identifies common errors.
Formats JSON with consistent two-space indentation.
Suggests fixes for trailing commas, single quotes, comments, and unquoted keys.
Guides conversion between JSON and YAML, TOML, CSV, and XML.
Analyzes top-level type, key names, nesting depth, and array sizes.
Suggests improvements for naming consistency, deep nesting, and large arrays.
limitations: It does not execute JSON or call external validators by itself.
It cannot guarantee business schema compliance unless the user supplies a schema.
Large or sensitive payloads should be reduced before sharing.
Format conversion may need manual review for complex arrays or mixed types.

use_cases.title: Fix API Test Payloads
use_cases.description: Find syntax problems in request or response bodies before a developer repeats an API test.

use_cases.title: Review Configuration Files
use_cases.description: Validate configuration data and explain strict JSON rules before deployment.

use_cases.title: Prepare Data Samples
use_cases.description: Format and inspect shared JSON samples so analysts can understand fields and nested structures.

prompt_templates.title: Validate JSON
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this JSON for syntax errors. Explain each issue with line references and suggest the smallest safe fix: [paste JSON]

prompt_templates.title: Format Payload
prompt_templates.prompt: Format this JSON with two-space indentation. Preserve all values and tell me if any syntax problem prevents formatting: [paste JSON]

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this JSON structure. Summarize the top-level type, key names, value types, array sizes, and nesting depth: [paste JSON]

prompt_templates.title: Convert With Type Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this JSON to [target format]. Preserve data types, flag ambiguous fields, and note any manual review needed: [paste JSON]

output_examples.input: A settings file with a trailing comma and single quoted values.
output_examples.output: Reports two syntax errors, explains the strict JSON rules, and describes the corrected version.

output_examples.input: A minified API response with nested arrays and metadata fields.
output_examples.output: Returns a readable formatting plan and summarizes the object shape, array sizes, and nesting depth.

output_examples.input: A customer export request that needs conversion from JSON to CSV.
output_examples.output: Explains how nested values should be flattened and flags fields that need manual mapping decisions.

best_practices: Validate syntax before formatting or converting content.
Ask before changing key order, removing comments, or rewriting structure.
Preserve data types and call out uncertain conversions.
anti_patterns: Do not assume commented or trailing-comma JSON is valid strict JSON.
Do not sort keys or remove fields without user approval.
Do not paste secrets or full production payloads when small samples are enough.

faq.question: Can this skill validate strict JSON?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on strict JSON syntax, including commas, quotes, comments, brackets, and unsupported values.

faq.question: Can it repair invalid JSON?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest corrections and provide a corrected version when the intended structure is clear.

faq.question: Does it use external commands?
faq.answer: The skill documentation does not require external command execution. It describes validation and formatting steps for the AI assistant.

faq.question: Can it validate against a schema?
faq.answer: It can help when you provide the schema. Without a schema, it can only review syntax and visible structure.

faq.question: Can it convert JSON to other formats?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives conversion guidance for formats such as YAML, TOML, CSV, and XML.

faq.question: Is it suitable for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use reduced samples when possible. Remove secrets, personal data, and production tokens before sharing content.
